source.title: Improving Generalization by Permutation Routing Across Model Copies

record.file_problem: Text includes the full paper through the beginning of the MLP appendix, but is cut off before the MLP experiment details and later appendices. Some extracted figure text is garbled; table and prose results remain readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a newly proposed message-routing training method on perceptrons, committee machines, and an MLP, reporting generalization errors against single-copy and replica-based baselines.
record.gate_note: The paper reports outcomes for its own M-cover routing intervention and baselines. Cited findings about replica methods, dropout, and spatial coupling are not treated as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates its own permutation-routing method, but none of its results tests V1–V8. Increasing the number of training copies is not a network-width sweep, and routing is not dropout. References to large batches, flat minima, and dropout supply context rather than tests.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate with one qualification: the authors report improvements over single-copy baselines in all three architectures, and over replica-based baselines only where those comparators are available. They describe the evaluation as a controlled proof of principle and defer broader benchmarks and hyperparameter sweeps.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces an additional M-cover message-routing construction and collapses trained copies at evaluation; applies the base learning dynamics on the routed graph. Perceptron uses simulated annealing, while committee and MLP use SGD variants.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization varies with Gaussian-ring kernel width and shift, cover count, and routing topology; structured routing is reported to outperform uniform routing in the perceptron, while committee results vary across a broad range of σ.

fits_no_version.finding: M-cover routing lowers reported mean generalization or test error relative to single-copy training in the three benchmarks; replica-based comparators are available only for the perceptron and committee machine. Gains depend on routing topology and cover count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Routing learning messages across model copies can improve held-out performance after collapsing the copies into a single predictor.

record.problems: The authors describe the benchmark as a controlled proof of principle, not an exhaustive evaluation; larger-scale benchmarks, broader architecture classes, and wider hyperparameter sweeps are deferred. Perceptron results use 20 trials; the committee table's trial count is not stated. Figure-only sweeps lack precise readable values in the supplied text. The supplied text cuts off during the MLP appendix.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted; eight rows retained.

untested.parts: No comparison of random-label fitting and held-out performance with natural-label training.
No network-width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No batch-size comparison or large-batch recipe intervention.
No dropout intervention; dropout appears only in discussion.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison of generalization measures.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, not denials of the reported routing gains. The supplied text includes MLP experimental details in Appendix A.3, contrary to the record's claim that it cuts off before those details.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorization or natural-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
